transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, thanks for seeing me. I’m not sure how to explain it without sounding… dramatic, maybe. But for a while now I’ve had this feeling—more than a feeling, honestly—that some people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are sort of keeping tabs on me.

Like, which clients I’m meeting with, where I show up, that kind of thing. And then I’ll notice little signals—an invitation that seems oddly timed, a panel topic that lines up too closely, even who ends up sitting near me at events. I do try to tell myself it could just be coincidence, and I know that’s probably what you’re hoping I’ll say, but I can’t really let it go. It’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this way—when did you first start noticing that people were watching or targeting you like this?

I guess… maybe around two months? It wasn’t like one clear day where I thought, “this is happening,” but that’s about when I started noticing the client meeting stuff and these little signals feeling connected.

I know two months isn’t, like, forever or anything, so maybe I’m over-reading it, but… it’s been pretty consistently on my mind since then.
Aside from these beliefs about being watched, have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people don't seem to notice?

I don’t think so, no. I mean… nothing like hearing voices talking to me or seeing people who aren’t there. Sometimes I’ll notice a sound or catch something out of the corner of my eye, but I assume that’s normal, right? I wouldn’t say I’ve had anything like that.
Over these past two months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or, on the other end, unusually energetic, elated, or needing much less sleep than usual?

I don’t think so, not in any extreme way. I mean, I’ve been stressed and kind of preoccupied, sure, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been hopeless or, like, unusually high-energy or anything. My sleep’s maybe not perfect, but… I think that’s just normal stress? I’m trying to answer that the right way.
Has this belief affected your ability to work, maintain relationships, or handle your daily responsibilities?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m still working, so it’s not like everything’s fallen apart or anything. But… my practice has gotten smaller, I guess. I’ve missed some follow-ups with clients, and I’ve avoided a few public panels I normally would’ve done.

I’m still handling the basics, but I’m not keeping up the same level of client contact I used to. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Do you have any medical conditions, recent illnesses, or use of medications, alcohol, or recreational drugs that might be relevant here?

I don’t think there’s anything major there. No medical condition that I know of, and I haven’t been sick recently in any way that seems connected. I’m not on anything unusual… and I’m not really using drugs or anything like that. Alcohol is not a big thing for me either.

I mean, if there’s something specific you’re looking for, I can try to think it through more carefully, but nothing jumps out to me.
Have you had any recent head injuries, seizures, or noticeable changes in your memory, concentration, or thinking clarity?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t had any head injuries or seizures or anything like that.

Memory and concentration… I mean, I have normal distracted moments, but nothing that feels like a big change or like I’m not thinking clearly. At least not that I’ve noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent, well-systematized belief of being watched and targeted by colleagues in her professional circles, without any accompanying hallucinations, disorganized speech, or significant mood episode symptoms (no mania, no depression). The belief has been present for approximately two months and has caused mild functional impairment (reduced client contact, avoidance of public panels) while leaving most daily functioning intact. The absence of hallucinations, thought disorder, or broader psychotic disorganization argues against schizophrenia (F20), and the lack of manic or depressive symptoms argues against a mood disorder with psychotic features (F30.2). The clinical picture—an isolated, non-bizarre persecutory delusion with preserved functioning aside from delusion-related avoidance—is most consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22), albeit with duration slightly short of the traditional 3-month threshold, warranting continued monitoring.
